data.title: Ipsen Advances Late-Stage Trial for New Wrinkle Treatment
data.description:
Ipsen (GB:0MH6) announced an update on their ongoing clinical study.

Study Overview: Ipsen is testing IPN10200, also called corabotase, in adults in China with moderate to severe lines between the eyebrows. The official title is “A Phase III, Multicentre, Double-blind, Randomised, Placebo-controlled, Parallel Group Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of IPN10200 in the Improvement of the Appearance of Moderate To Severe Glabellar Lines in Adult Chinese Participants.”

The study will assess whether one dose improves the appearance of these lines and remains safe over time. The trial is important because positive results could support Ipsen’s expansion in the large and competitive market for wrinkle treatments.

Intervention/Treatment: Participants receive one local injection of corabotase, a biological treatment, or a placebo with no active drug. Corabotase is intended to reduce the appearance of glabellar lines by acting on selected muscles between the eyebrows.

Study Design: This is a Phase III treatment study with participants assigned at random to either corabotase or placebo. Participants, study doctors, and those assessing results are not told which treatment was given, helping reduce bias.

Study Timeline: The registry does not list a study start date, primary completion date, or estimated completion date. The record was first submitted on August 19, 2026, and was last updated on November 19, 2026, showing that recruitment information remains active.

The study is recruiting and each participant may be followed for up to 55 weeks after the single injection. That long follow-up should provide information on both the treatment’s durability and its safety, although no study results have been posted.

Market Implications: The update offers limited immediate evidence for Ipsen’s stock, since it reports trial progress rather than clinical results. Still, continued recruitment in a late-stage study may support investor confidence in Ipsen’s aesthetic medicine pipeline.

Investor sentiment will likely depend on future efficacy, safety, and regulatory updates. The treatment is entering a crowded wrinkle-care market, where competition from established injectable products means clear benefits and reliable results will be important.

The study is ongoing and was updated on the ClinicalTrials portal, where further details are available.

To learn more about GB:0MH6’s potential, visit the Ipsen drug pipeline page.

data.title: Bama Tea Says Military Procurement Qualification Suspension Is Limited
data.description:
Bama Tea Co. Ltd. Class H ( (HK:6980) ) has shared an update.

Bama Tea Co., Ltd. is a joint stock company incorporated in the People’s Republic of China with limited liability; the release provides no further information on its industry, products, services or market focus.

data.title: Company Denies Share Manipulation Allegations, Says Measure Is Personal
data.description:
Altinkilic Gida ve Sut Sanayi Ticaret AS ( (TR:ALKLC) ) has issued an announcement.

Altinkilic Gida ve Sut Sanayi Ticaret AS said allegations that its officers and controlling shareholders manipulated company shares and made substantial profits were false. The company said management had no knowledge of or involvement in share-price movements, which it characterized as occurring through normal market dynamics.

It said officers and controlling shareholders had invested personal savings in an independent fund, where part of the principal was lost. The company said an Istanbul Chief Public Prosecutor’s Office precautionary measure applies to personal accounts that, according to social-media reports, appear to arise from that fund, and not to the company, its commercial activities or corporate bank accounts.

data.title: Four Seas Mercantile Accepts Ten-Year Premises Lease Offer
data.description:
Four Seas Mercantile Holdings Limited ( (HK:0374) ) has shared an update.

An indirect wholly owned subsidiary accepted the lessor’s offer on 20 November 2026 to rent premises for 10 years, with a stated commencement date of 15 February 2027 or another date specified by the lessor, and an option to renew for a further five years subject to approval. The accepted offer forms a legally binding contract until superseded by the lease, and the subsidiary must execute the lease and admission application within one month after receiving the relevant documents.

Under HKFRS 16, the Group will recognise a right-of-use asset with an unaudited value estimated at approximately HK$377 million, subject to final audit. Because the applicable percentage ratios exceed 25% but remain below 100%, the transaction is classified as a major transaction under the Listing Rules; written approval from shareholders holding approximately 56.81% of the company was accepted in lieu of a general meeting.

data.title: CARsgen Reports Preliminary Clinical Data for In Vivo CAR T Candidate CT1182
data.description:
CARsgen Therapeutics Holdings Ltd. ( (HK:2171) ) just unveiled an announcement.

CARsgen reported preliminary clinical data for CT1182, an in vivo CD19/CD20-targeting CAR T-cell candidate for relapsed/refractory B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma, developed on its CARvivo® platform. As of October 31, 2026, six patients with aggressive, Stage IV lymphoma subtypes had been enrolled; among six efficacy-evaluable patients, three achieved complete response and two partial response, with all responses ongoing at the cutoff date.

Among six DLT-evaluable patients, no treatment-related serious adverse events, dose-limiting toxicities or infusion-related reactions were observed; no ICANS, IEC-HS or infusion-associated biphasic cytokine elevation was reported, and only Grade 1 CRS occurred. The company said the early data showed effective gene delivery, encouraging efficacy at low doses and a safety profile supporting outpatient administration, while complete B-cell aplasia in responders suggested possible use in other B-cell diseases.

data.title: PTC Inc. Divestiture Risks: Operational Challenges and Market Reactions Threaten Valuation and Growth
data.description:

PTC Inc. faces execution risk when divesting businesses or assets, as complex operational separation, potential disruption to remaining revenue streams, and unanticipated liabilities can erode the expected strategic and financial gains. Such challenges may impair its business performance and long‑term prospects, particularly if management attention is diverted and key personnel or customers are lost.

The company is also exposed to capital‑markets risk, since investors or analysts may view specific divestitures unfavorably or perceive sale prices as inadequate, prompting share disposals and a negative reassessment of its outlook. data.title: ATRenew Earnings Call Highlights Strong Growth and Expansion
data.description:
ATRenew Inc. Sponsored ADR ((RERE)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

ATRenew’s third-quarter earnings call carried a strongly positive tone, with management highlighting faster revenue and operating profit growth, better margins, expanding retail operations, overseas gains, and ample liquidity. Seasonal softness, weaker new-device shipments, higher inventory, rising costs, and slower overseas activity were acknowledged, but expense ratios improved and growth expectations remained firm.

Revenue and Operating Profit Accelerate

ATRenew reported third-quarter revenue of RMB6.45 billion, up 25.3% from a year earlier and above the high end of its guidance. Non-GAAP operating profit rose 50.7% to more than RMB210 million, while the operating margin expanded 55 basis points to 3.3%.

Product and Service Revenue Both Increase

Net product revenue grew 27.0% to RMB6 billion, supported mainly by online sales of pre-owned consumer electronics. Net service revenue increased 6.1% to RMB400 million, driven by the PJT Marketplace and multi-category recycling services.

Higher Margins and a Stronger Retail Mix

The 1P business gross margin improved to 14.4% from 13.4% a year earlier. Management credited high-efficiency C2B recycling, compliant refurbishment capabilities, and a broader retail mix, with 1P2C revenue rising to 41.4% of product revenue from 36.4%.

1P and Retail Expansion Continue

ATRenew continued to prioritize its self-operated 1P business, with 1P2C retail revenue increasing 44.3% year over year. Its share of product revenue rose by five percentage points, showing that retail is becoming a larger part of the company’s business.

Store and Door-to-Door Network Expands

As of September 30, ATRenew operated 2,130 stores in 303 cities, nine more than at the end of June. Its door-to-door service team exceeded 2,600 employees at quarter-end and reached more than 2,800 by the end of October, supporting long-term goals of 5,000 stores and 5,000 service members.

More Flexible Fulfillment Capacity

The company shifted its door-to-door staffing model toward a larger share of flexible capacity that can be trained and deployed quickly. Management said the change improved fulfillment flexibility while helping optimize related expenses.

Refurbishment Revenue Posts Strong Growth

Revenue from refurbished products increased 34.6% year over year, reflecting the growing role of compliant refurbishment. On-demand refurbishment represented more than 40% of that business and created virtual inventory for sale without adding pressure from unsold refurbished goods.

PJT Adds AI Tools for Merchants

PJT integrated AI models and intelligent trading tools to help sellers develop more effective pricing strategies. Its 3P warehousing inspection penetration reached 85.3%, up about 6.7 percentage points year over year, while new tools supported buyer sourcing and the Like-new device marketplace.

PJT Merchant Base Reaches 2.52 Million

The marketplace continued building its specialty buyer model and expanding into fragmented and lower-tier markets. Registered PJT merchants totaled 2.52 million at the end of September, giving the platform a broader base for future transaction growth.

Paipai Shows Platform Improvement

Paipai required fewer subsidies to support merchant activity, while B2C platform service revenue rose significantly from the previous quarter. The platform is focusing on attracting more small and medium-sized merchants, improving transaction experiences, and strengthening price competitiveness.

Multi-Category Recycling Gains Momentum

Revenue from multi-category recycling services grew 38% year over year in the third quarter, and the company operated 971 stores. A designer-toys-themed store opened in September after a racquet-sports location launched in May, with both stores performing better than management expected.

Themed Store Pilot Program Expands

ATRenew plans to continue small-scale themed-store pilots in Shanghai and test categories such as billiards cues, ski equipment, camera gear, and bags and luggage. Management expects the network to reach 10 themed stores by the end of 2026.

International Revenue Surges

Overseas product revenue reached RMB240 million in the quarter, up 150% year over year and equal to 4% of 1P product revenue. ATRenew continued building sales channels in Dubai, where its office began trial operations in October, and expects overseas revenue to reach RMB1 billion for the full year.

Expense Ratios Improve Despite Higher Spending

Absolute operating expenses increased, but several expense ratios moved in the right direction. Non-GAAP fulfillment costs fell to 7.9% of revenue from 8.4%, selling and marketing costs declined to 6.9% from 7.0%, and research and development costs dropped to 1.0% from 1.2%, while general and administrative costs held at 1.3%.

Liquidity Supports Investment and Buybacks

Cash, restricted cash, short-term investments, and funds receivable from payment providers totaled RMB1.94 billion at September 30, 2026. The company repurchased about 1.6 million ADS for roughly US$6.6 million during the quarter and had approximately US$28.6 million remaining under its current buyback authorization.

Hong Kong Listing Application Submitted

ATRenew confidentially submitted an application for a Main Board listing on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. Management said a listing could improve access to Hong Kong’s capital markets and broaden the investor base, although approval remains subject to the required filing and review process.

Long-Term Capability Building Remains a Priority

Management said it will continue investing in the self-operated 1P business and develop the AHS Recycle brand from a recycling service into a retail platform. Other priorities include fulfillment, supply chain, overseas B2B operations, compliant exports, recycling platforms, and automation technology.

Seasonal Third-Quarter Softness

Management described the third quarter as a traditionally slower period for the pre-owned electronics industry. Recycling volumes tend to be lower than in the second and fourth quarters as flagship devices begin launching late in the period, while limited consumer promotions can weigh on retail activity.

New-Device Shipments Decline Across the Industry

Rapidly rising memory prices contributed to higher prices for new smartphones, laptops, tablets, and other electronics. Management also cited changes in product launch timing and said overall new-device shipments declined year over year, creating a more difficult industry backdrop.

Inventory Rises as the Business Expands

Inventory stood at RMB1.31 billion at the end of September, down about RMB80 million from June but up approximately RMB240 million from the end of 2025. The increase reflected wider self-operated recycling and trading activity, higher pre-owned device prices, and the slower turnover typical of growing 1P2C retail operations.

Overseas Revenue Eases Sequentially

Third-quarter overseas revenue was slightly below the seasonally strong second quarter. Management attributed the decline to slower China-sourced supply and softer overseas B2B trading activity, even as international revenue remained well ahead of the prior year.

Operating Costs Rise in Absolute Terms

Non-GAAP fulfillment expenses increased 17.2% to RMB510 million, while selling and marketing expenses rose 23.6% to RMB450 million. General and administrative expenses grew 27.0% to RMB94 million and research and development expenses increased 10.0% to RMB72 million, mainly because of higher personnel costs.

Management Reviews the 2027 Operating Environment

ATRenew is preparing its 2027 budget while watching macroeconomic conditions, consumer trends, and the effect of lower new-device shipments on recycling supply. Store openings and door-to-door expansion will be adjusted according to city tiers and seasonal demand.

Revenue Growth Guidance Remains Strong

For the fourth quarter, ATRenew expects revenue of RMB7.78 billion to RMB7.88 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 24.4% to 26.0%. Full-year 2026 revenue is expected to reach RMB27.03 billion to RMB27.11 billion, up 28.3% to 28.8%, while overseas revenue is projected at RMB1 billion.

Long-Term Targets Stay in Place

The company maintained its long-term goals of 5,000 stores and a 5,000-member door-to-door service team nationwide. It also expects to have 10 themed stores by the end of 2026 and said it is preparing for healthy long-term growth and greater trading penetration in 2027.

ATRenew’s call combined strong quarterly execution with clear investment in retail, refurbishment, logistics, technology, and international operations. While seasonal demand, industry shipment declines, inventory growth, and higher costs remain risks, improving margins, strong liquidity, rapid revenue growth, and stable guidance gave the quarter an encouraging profile for investors.

data.title: SSC Announces Contracts for Two 7,000-CEU Dual-Fuel Car Carriers
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from Singapore Shipping Corporation Limited ( (SG:S19) ).

Singapore Shipping Corporation Limited is an Asian shipping group active in shipowning, ship management, ship agency, terminal operations and logistics services. It has specialised in owning and chartering PCTCs for 18 years, with established expertise in the international car-carrier segment.

SSC has entered into shipbuilding contracts with GSI and CSTC for two 7,000-CEU PCTCs, at a total estimated acquisition cost of approximately US$210 million. The contracts form part of a fleet-renewal programme focused on modern, efficient and environmentally responsible car carriers, with LNG dual-fuel propulsion providing greater fuel flexibility and improved emissions performance than conventional-fuel vessels.
